aiOverview.content: You can upload custom consumption interval data in OpenSolar by following the official process on the project energy tab How to upload interval data – OpenSolar.Open Project: Navigate to your project in OpenSolar.Go to Energy Tab: Select the Energy tab from the project menu.Select Data Source: Expand the Data Source dropdown and select Interval Data under Electricity Usage.Upload CSV: Click Upload CSV and select your prepared file.CSV File Guidelines & FormatsOfficial Templates: Use the official unedited templates provided by OpenSolar rather than custom structural layouts.Interval Structures: Supports vertical or horizontal structures with 15, 30, or 60-minute intervals.Data Preparation: Match headers directly to the downloaded template, align start dates accurately, and confirm measurement units (kWh) after uploading.Partial or Cross-Year Datasets: OpenSolar accepts partial or cross-year datasets and automatically extrapolates missing periods, though very large datasets may experience processing delays.If you are running into a specific error or formatting issue with your CSV file, let me know what interval length (15, 30, or 60 min) you are using or what error message appears so I can help troubleshoot it.If you are running into a specific error or formatting issue with your CSV file, let me know what interval length (15, 30, or 60 min) you are using or what error message appears so I can help troubleshoot it.AI responses may include mistakes. aiOverview.content: In NREL's System Advisor Model (SAM), electric load data and weather files do not account for Daylight Saving Time (DST).No Daylight Saving Time: SAM assumes all time series data (load, weather, and time-of-use electricity pricing) operates on a standard, non-shifting local time (e.g., standard time year-round). If your raw CSV load data includes DST spring-forward (8,759 rows) or fall-back (8,761 rows) shifts, you must flatten or adjust the timestamp series to a continuous 8,760-hour (or exact sub-hourly equivalent) standard time format before importing.Time Step & Row Counts:For hourly data, SAM expects 8,760 values for a standard non-leap year (plus an extra header row at the top).For sub-hourly data, you must specify the corresponding time step (e.g., enter 15 for 15-minute data), requiring 8,760 × (steps per hour) rows (e.g., 35,040 rows for 15-minute intervals).Start Convention: SAM assumes the dataset starts on Monday, January 1, with the first row representing the end of the first time step (e.g., the hour ending at 1:00 AM on January 1).Time-of-Use (TOU) Alignment: If your utility rate structure uses time-dependent or seasonal pricing, your electric load CSV and weather/rate profiles must share the exact same time convention so weekdays, weekends, and peak periods match accurately.You can manage or inspect these settings via the Electric Load Input Documentation or by exporting a default template directly inside SAM.You can manage or inspect these settings via the Electric Load Input Documentation or by exporting a default template directly inside SAM.If you are converting a raw utility CSV with DST shifts, let me know:What interval your data is in (hourly, 15-minute, etc.)Where the data is located (which region/utility)I can help guide you on how to shift or interpolate the missing/extra hours.If you are converting a raw utility CSV with DST shifts, let me know:I can help guide you on how to shift or interpolate the missing/extra hours.AI responses may include mistakes.
